1→# Ryde — Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution
   2→
   3→Entry for the **Tencent Cloud "AI CAN DO IT" Hackathon Singapore 2026**, Digital Native track
   4→(the Ryde challenge statement, section 5 of the organisers' document).
   5→
   6→**Status: the system runs end to end on the real Tencent Cloud model (ADP), with the
   7→deterministic mock as the default for a fresh checkout.** The scope is ruled: a two-category MVP
   8→(route deviation + no-show charge) with three agents, a deterministic evidence layer, and an
   9→observable case-file view. The challenge statement is in
  10→[`docs/statement-extract.md`](docs/statement-extract.md); the builder's contract is in
  11→[`CODEBUDDY.md`](CODEBUDDY.md).
  12→
  13→## Start here
  14→
  15→- **Try it without a key:** [Run](#run). A new server from the standard launchers uses the deterministic mock; an existing Ryde server is reused as it is.
  16→- **Use approved Tencent access:** [Local live-copy guide](docs/live-copy.md). The live launchers are separate and need a private sidecar.
  17→- **Inspect the design:** [Architecture](docs/architecture.md), [policy](docs/policy.md) and [dataset](docs/dataset.md).
  18→- **Inspect development evidence:** [Conversation history](evidence/conversation-history/README.md) and [screenshots and API-call records](evidence/). CodeBuddy development usage and Tencent demo-call evidence are separate records.
  19→
  20→This is a local demonstration with synthetic trip data, not a connection to Ryde's production
  21→accounts or payment systems. It records decisions; it does not transfer money.
  22→
  23→## The challenge
  24→
  25→Ride-hailing platforms process thousands of dispute tickets daily: fare disputes, route deviations,
  26→property damage, safety incidents, no-show charges. They are subjective, emotionally charged, and
  27→currently resolved by humans reviewing GPS telemetry, chat logs, payment records and company policy
  28→by hand. The result is slow, expensive and inconsistent.
  29→
  30→The task is an autonomous multi-agent system that gathers evidence, builds both sides' cases, applies
  31→company policy and issues a fair ruling with a confidence score and a plain-language explanation.
  32→
  33→## Architecture
  34→
  35→Three core agents, all MVP-required:
  36→
  37→| Agent | Role |
  38→|---|---|
  39→| **Rider Advocate** | Builds the rider's case from the Evidence Pack and the policy |
  40→| **Driver Advocate** | Builds the driver's case from the Evidence Pack and the policy |
  41→| **Judge** | Weighs both cases, applies policy, rules, and explains the reasoning with a confidence score |
  42→
  43→Inter-agent communication must be **observable** — a judge needs to see how the agents exchange
  44→information and build their cases. That surface is a required deliverable, not a nice-to-have.
  45→
  46→The full walkthrough — components, lifecycle, gates, observability — is in
  47→[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md). The system on one page:
  48→
  49→```mermaid
  50→flowchart TD
  51→    PACK["Dataset pack"] --> B["Server"]
  52→    PACK --> CL["Command-line runner"]
  53→    A["Rider and driver intake forms"] --> B
  54→    B --> C{"Category in scope?"}
  55→    CL --> C
  56→    C -- "Out of scope" --> H["Human review"]
  57→    C -- "Route deviation or no-show" --> E["Evidence Pack"]
  58→    POL["Policy document"] --> RA["Rider Advocate"]
  59→    POL --> DA["Driver Advocate"]
  60→    POL --> J["Judge"]
  61→    E --> RA
  62→    E --> DA
  63→    RA --> S{"Questions for the party?"}
  64→    DA --> S
  65→    S -- "Yes, first round" --> O4["Needs info"]
  66→    O4 --> PA["Party answers follow-ups"]
  67→    PA -- "Fresh run with the answers" --> B
  68→    S -- "No" --> J
  69→    J --> G{"Gates pass? Confidence, cap, measured deviation, NS-6, NS-8, RD-5, RD-4"}
  70→    G -- "Yes" --> O1["Ruled"]
  71→    G -- "No" --> O2["Withheld"]
  72→    O2 -- "Candidate ruling queued" --> H
  73→    J -- "Model could not answer" --> H
  74→    B -. "Every step emits an event" .-> L["Event log"]
  75→    J -.-> L
  76→    L -- "Embedded in the case file" --> K["Operator console"]
  77→```
  78→
  79→## Documents
  80→
  81→- [`docs/statement-extract.md`](docs/statement-extract.md) — the challenge statement, verbatim
  82→- [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) — architecture diagram and system description
  83→- [`docs/policy.md`](docs/policy.md) — the policy rule set the Judge applies, with per-rule provenance
  84→- [`docs/dataset.md`](docs/dataset.md) — the labelled corpus, its provenance and its limitations
  85→- [`docs/prompts.md`](docs/prompts.md) — how the prompts drive each agent, and what code checks after the model answers
  86→- [`docs/replay.md`](docs/replay.md) — the static replay of a recorded run: how it is exported and what it shows
  87→- [`docs/evidence-plan.md`](docs/evidence-plan.md) — development-process evidence rules
  88→- [`docs/tool-experiences.md`](docs/tool-experiences.md) — running log of how the development tools behaved
  89→- [`docs/build-briefs/`](docs/build-briefs/) — the brief each CodeBuddy build session worked from, kept as a record of the process
  90→- [`CODEBUDDY.md`](CODEBUDDY.md) — builder's entry point and project memory
  91→
  92→## Development tooling
  93→
  94→Built with Tencent Cloud **CodeBuddy**. The competition mandates proof of product usage, so
  95→development happens in the tool and evidence is captured as it occurs.
  96→
  97→## Run
  98→
  99→### One-click start
 100→
 101→Double-click **`start.command`** (macOS) or **`start.bat`** (Windows). That is the whole setup:
 102→Python 3.9 or newer is the only requirement, and no API key is needed, because the demo runs on
 103→the deterministic mock.
 104→
 105→The launcher picks a free port and opens `http://127.0.0.1:8000/start/` — the start page, which
 106→links to the party and operator surfaces. If port 8000 is busy it reuses a Ryde demo already running there;
 107→otherwise it tries 8001 to 8010 and uses the first free one. If you already started the demo
 108→yourself, the launcher reuses that copy as it is. The terminal window stays open while the demo
 109→runs: closing it (or pressing Ctrl+C in it) stops the server, while closing only the browser tab
 110→does not.
 111→
 112→A macOS ZIP download may need System Settings, Privacy & Security, **Open Anyway** for the first
 113→double-click. Windows SmartScreen may need **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
 114→
 115→### Manual start (fallback)
 116→
 117→No dependencies: it runs on a stock Python 3.9+ with the standard library only, using a
 118→deterministic mock in place of the LLM. Start the server and open the pages:
 119→
 120→```bash
 121→python3 -m app.server --llm mock
 122→```
 123→
 124→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/start/` is the entry page
 125→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` is the operator console (case files, the review queue, human decisions)
 126→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/` is the rider's dispute form, which links to the driver form and the status page
 127→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/driver-filing.html` is the driver's dispute form
 128→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/status.html` looks up a filing by its reference number
 129→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/driver.html` is the read-only sample driver account
 130→- `python3 -m app.server --llm mock --port 8011` serves the same pages on another port
 131→
 132→Use the port printed by the launcher if it is not 8000.
 133→
 134→### Live start (approved access only)
 135→
 136→Double-click **`start-live.command`** (macOS) or **`start-live.bat`** (Windows). This selects
 137→Tencent ADP explicitly, needs internet access and uses credits. Follow the
 138→[live-copy guide](docs/live-copy.md) to supply the private `.env.live` sidecar. No key is
 139→included in the public source.
 140→
 141→The live launcher uses port **8030** by default, opens the rider form rather than `/start/`,
 142→and prints the actual party, operator and status URLs. It refuses an occupied port and
 143→does not silently fall back to the mock. If private access is unavailable, use the standard
 144→keyless launchers instead and label the result as mock.
 145→
 146→### Tests and command-line cases
 147→
 148→To run the tests and single cases from the command line:
 149→
 150→```bash
 151→python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
 152→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0101
 153→python3 -m app.cli --pack organiser-style-v1 --dispute DISP-002
 154→```
 155→
 156→Live evaluation uses credits and requires approved access; it is not needed for the keyless demo.
 157→The evaluation harness replays every labelled case — `python3 -m app.eval --llm tencent --repeat 3` —
 158→and scores the rulings against the labels, answering a round-one stop and running it again.
 159→
 160→`--dispute` takes either a dispute id inside the selected pack or a path to a record file
 161→(`python3 -m app.cli --dispute data/packs/ryde-synth-v1/disputes/RD-0101.json`). The pack
 162→defaults to `dataset_pack` in `app/config.json`; `--pack` overrides it for one run.
 163→
 164→That prints the agent-to-agent event strip and the ruling, and writes the run's artifacts to
 165→`runs/<run_id>/`: `events.jsonl` (the observable traffic), `payloads/*.json` (the full payload
 166→behind each event) and `case_file.json` (evidence, both claims, resolution).
 167→
 168→The rider form is `/party/index.html`; the driver form is `/party/driver-filing.html`.
 169→Both use the shared form script and the same filing API. Save the reference number for
 170→`/party/status.html#reference-input`, which recovers questions and the current outcome.
 171→The rider demo list contains rider filings only. The read-only driver account at
 172→`/party/driver.html` is fixed to D-2009, including T-RD0109; filings on other sample drivers'
 173→trips need reference lookup and do not appear in that account. The forms are local demos,
 174→not signed-in accounts. Entering an amount is a request, not a payment.
 175→
 176→The corpus lives in two swappable packs under `data/packs/`: `ryde-synth-v1` (our 17 labelled
 177→cases, our record shape) and `organiser-style-v1` (the same 17 cases as twins in the organisers'
 178→shape, plus the organisers' own `DISP-002` verbatim). `RD-0103` is a deviation too small to matter. `NS-0203` is a driver who marked arrival 885 m
 179→from the pickup point. `RD-0109` is a remedy above the autonomous cap that the system refuses to
 180→issue on its own. `OS-0301` is an out-of-scope filing routed to human review without an LLM call. `docs/dataset.md` maps each case
 181→to what it tests; `<pack>/ground-truth.json` holds the expected outcomes, deliberately kept out
 182→of the records the agents see.
 183→
 184→Seven gates stand between a ruling and the parties, and **all seven are enforced in Python, not
 185→asked of the model in a prompt**. The confidence threshold is one of them, and so is ESC-4's SGD
 186→50 autonomous cap. ESC-2 withholds a route-case ruling when the deviation cannot be measured or the
 187→fare charged cannot be established. NS-6 withholds a contested no-show unless the ruling is a
 188→refund of exactly the fee for a low fee and a clean rider record. NS-8 withholds a no-show refund
 189→larger than the recorded fee, any compensation on a no-show case, or any refund whose fee the
 190→record cannot prove. RD-5 withholds a route ruling that refunds less than the overcharge the
 191→records prove. RD-4 withholds a route refund larger than the records prove the rider overpaid (a
 192→fixed fare paid as quoted proves nothing) and any compensation on a route case. Each gate
 193→withholds the ruling for a human; none of them rewrites what the Judge proposed.
 194→Try them:
 195→
 196→```bash
 197→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0109   # withheld: above the cap
 198→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0108   # withheld: no deviation to measure
 199→```
 200→
 201→**Mock by default.** The default provider is a deterministic mock. Its free-text fields (claim
 202→summaries, arguments, the Judge's explanation) are prefixed `MOCK`; actions, amounts, rule IDs and
 203→evidence refs are not. A mock run is a plumbing demonstration, never a real ruling. The real model is
 204→Tencent Cloud ADP, one app per agent: put the three app keys in `.env` (see `.env.example`), then
 205→run `python3 -m app.server --llm tencent` or `python3 -m app.cli --llm tencent --dispute <id>`.
 206→
 207→## How this was built
 208→
 209→The code in `app/` and `ui/` was written in Tencent Cloud CodeBuddy. A planning agent wrote each
 210→session's brief and its failing tests first; CodeBuddy built until they passed, and the result was
 211→re-checked by running it, not by describing it. The screenshots in `evidence/` record those
 212→sessions as they happened.
 213→
